title: Specify `SecurityError` when `requestLEScan()` lacks transient user activation
body:
The Web Bluetooth Scanning specification is ambiguous about how to handle a missing transient user activation when calling `navigator.bluetooth.requestLEScan()`.

In the summary note for [`requestLEScan()`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/scanning.html#scanning), the specification states:

>  Additionally, UAs are likely to require a transient user activation on its relevant global object when `requestLEScan` is called.

However, the algorithm steps for `requestLEScan()` do not include an explicit step checking for transient user activation, nor do they specify which `DOMException` should be returned if the required activation is missing.

In contrast, the algorithm for [`requestDevice()`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#device-discovery) explicitly defines this check in step 4:

> Check that the algorithm is triggered while its relevant global object has a transient activation, otherwise throw a `SecurityError` and abort these steps.

Could the specification add an explicit step to `requestLEScan()` to check for transient user activation and reject with a `SecurityError` DOMException, matching `requestDevice()` to resolve this ambiguity?
